title: Tuʻi Tonga maritime chiefdom (Tuʻi Tonga empire)
summary: The Tuʻi Tonga was the paramount title of a Tongan maritime chiefdom, often called an empire, centred on Tongatapu. Tongan oral tradition traces it to about 950 CE, and the title-holders held authority over the dispersed Tonga Group in the second millennium CE, influencing Samoa, east Fiji and Wallis/ʻUvea. The capital moved from Heketā to Lapaha at Muʻa, where about 22 royal tombs (langi) survive.

uncertainty.note: Start is the 950 CE date from oral tradition and genealogies cited in Tonga's UNESCO tentative-list nomination; end follows its phrasing "from the tenth century to the eighteenth century" (taken as year 1800; the 18th century ends in 1800). The nomination also dates a few Lapaha tombs to 1250-1380 CE.

reviewer_note: Start date is oral tradition (950 CE) from Tonga's nomination text; the capital sequence (Heketā, then Lapaha around the 13th century) is from the same nomination and sources elsewhere disagree on details. Samoa and the empire's decline are not covered on the opened pages and are left out. The nomination text was prepared for the Tonga National Commission for UNESCO. Wikidata's Lapaha point may be a village centre.
